ai_summary: Scotland continues to demonstrate its vital role in Great Britain's energy mix, though transmission bottlenecks prevent consumers from fully realising its low-carbon potential. Current system operations show estimated Scottish wind output at 2.4 GW, which represents 23.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity, contributing significantly to the overall GB wind output of 5.1 GW. This strong regional renewable performance has suppressed Scottish carbon intensity to an exceptional 4 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to the GB-wide carbon intensity of 193 gCO2/kWh. Nevertheless, due to structural cross-border network limitations, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 15.6 GWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, accumulating a constraint cost of about £632,186. Because this green power cannot reach southern demand centres, thermal units have been ramped up, resulting in an estimated 2,968,142 m3 of gas burned elsewhere and 5,468 tonnes of CO2 emitted. Extrapolating these constraint patterns indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of approximately £231 million. This balancing expenditure flows directly into system network charges, resulting in an estimated increase of around £1/MWh on everybody's invoice in the UK.
